name: inprocess-obi-apb-pulp-i2c-two-step-clear-negative-f5
notes: Negative probe for the ordered-clear form, on the same real PULP apb_i2c level interrupt (configs/peripherals/pulp_i2c_irq).

The declared sequence is CMD=0 then CMD=0: two declared writes that never set the iack bit (apb_i2c.sv:128 `wire iack = r_cmd[0];`), so irq_flag stays set (apb_i2c.sv:189-193) and interrupt_o = irq_flag && s_ien never drops.

Expected result: the handler re-enters, the take limit is reached, the level is reported still high (level_stuck 1) and the case is failed. This is what makes the two-step form's pass condition non-vacuous: a declared clear that does not deassert the device is a recorded failure, not a pass.
This file declares the scenario; the real RTL run under runs/p1-irq/ is the evidence.
description: Negative probe for the ordered-clear form: the same PULP I2C level interrupt with a declared two-write sequence that never asserts iack, so the declared clear cannot deassert the device and the case must fail with level_stuck.
